newsitem.title: USA: Tornadoes hit Tennessee, Kentucky, 2 feared dead.
newsitem.headline: Tornadoes hit Tennessee, Kentucky, 2 feared dead.

text.p: One person was killed and another feared dead after more than a dozen tornadoes touched down in Tennessee and Kentucky late Friday and early Saturday, state emergency officials said.
One man was killed in Hammonville, Kentucky, as up to five tornadoes ploughed through the western half of the state, according to Hart County Judge Executive Terry Shelton.
Another man was feared dead near Chattanooga after 11 tornadoes ripped through Tennessee, said Tom Womack, spokesman for the Tennessee Emergency Management Agency.
"We had reports of one fatality but that has not been confirmed," he said. "As many as 50 people were hospitalized, 19 to 20 are still in the hospital and at least two are in critical condition."
The worst damage was reported near Chattanooga where a tornado cut a mile-wide swath through the city and suburbs and struck two apartment complexes housing about 3,000 people.
At least 60 people sought emergency shelter overnight and about 20,000 were without power early Saturday, Womack said. East Brainerd, a suburb of Chattanooga, was the hardest hit.
"As far as we can determine, a single tornado touched down in East Brainerd and apparently travelled about eight miles with the width of the damage being one mile wide," Womack said.

Federal emergency management agency officials, already in Tennessee for flood relief efforts, were helping state teams but there had been no official request for federal assistance, said Karen Grossman, media affairs officer with the federal emergency management agency in Nashville.
Meteorologists said the worst weather had passed and forecasts called for only isolated storms across Kentucky on Sunday.
